chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Frances Wayne, Ralph Burns and Woody Herman raiding his bands
summary: Frances Wayne joined in 1943, recorded Old Black Magic, and Woody Herman later took both her and Ralph Burns; Barnet says he enjoyed building bands.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: And how about Frances and Neal, when did they work for you? Frances Wayne and Neal Hefti?

Well, Frances worked for me in '43. She was in that band. But she was there -- she wasn't there at the Park Central. Virginia Maxie was there. Frances joined the band -- she was there when Ralph Burns was with the band. Oh, wait a minute. Ralph Burns was there. It wasn't Dodo, Dodo came a little later. Ralph was still in the band there. Because I had heard her with her brother's band, and Ralph had been playing in that, and I wound up with both of them. And then Woody Herman stole Ralph from me, and then he wound up

with Frances. I used to break bands up. I mean it got -- it was -- of course at that time, I mean, I had a reason. I told you about the draft board, you know. It was a very uneasy thing. But I think I got my kicks out of building bands.
Well, at times. Sometimes they didn't turn out too well. But some turned out better than others. Let's put it that way.
Did Frances ever record with you?
Yeah. She made, 'Old Black Magic,' with me.
Oh, of course. She was a beautiful singer, and person.
